record.file_problem: This is a repository record, not a full study text. The README and a partial file listing are provided; the code and linked documentation were not read or run. The provided text is not visibly garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal outcomes after automatic weight-edit abliteration on released models. This bears on practical removal (V2), but the reported per-layer weight-kernel edits are not the original study’s direct activation ablation and addition tests.
record.gate_note: The README describes difference-of-means directions, per-layer weight edits, and optional multi-direction ablation, but those descriptions alone are not results. Only the reported refusal outcomes after abliteration are recorded. No outcome is reported for adding a direction or for the optional multi-direction setting. The README mentions partial results for Phi-4-mini-instruct and Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat in an external log but gives no result values for them here.
record.test_reason: The README reports refusal counts on released instruct models before and after an automatic abliteration weight edit, which bears directly on V2. The method is Heretic's: per-layer difference-of-means directions, a per-layer weight kernel and a TPE search over edit parameters. It is not the original's single-direction orthogonalisation, so this is T2. No activation ablation, addition, jailbreak, multi-direction, transfer or reasoning-model results are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README presents ditch as a from-scratch, CPU-only rebuild of Heretic's abliteration method and credits Heretic and Arditi et al. It reports refusal reductions with low KL on a few small models. It stresses that the numbers come from one machine and are 'a data point, not a spec'. It states that ditch and Heretic have close Pareto fronts, with Heretic faster and ditch using less RAM. It makes no mechanistic claim.
record.recipe_differences: The README says ditch rebuilds Heretic's method: difference-of-means directions, per-layer weight kernels, and multi-objective search. Its reported results are weight edits, not direct activation projection at every layer and position or addition of the direction. Repository type: tool; described as a from-scratch Zig rebuild of Heretic.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary across model checkpoints. The README also notes different trial counts for Qwen3-0.6B and SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct.
record.problems: The README says the benchmark numbers were measured on one machine. Results cover only a few models, and two of the three main model results used 10 trials. No uncertainty estimates or direct general-capability evaluation are reported. The linked detailed log is not included in the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The README refers to partial results for Phi-4-mini-instruct and Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat in tools/real-model-validation.md but supplies no values for those results in the provided text.

untested.parts: General-capability retention beyond best-trial KL divergence. Larger and other released models: Phi-4-mini and Qwen1.5-MoE results are only in an external log. Uncertainty and repeat runs. Prompts held out from those used to select the trial.
Activation ablation, refusal induction by adding the direction, and capability retention; none are reported.
The multi-direction option (--n-directions) exists, but no results are reported for it.

record.verdict_notes: This is a tool README, not a study. It has no controls, no uncertainty and no capability benchmark beyond KL. Reported values are best trials from a search that optimises refusals on the evaluation prompts, so they likely overstate held-out removal. The context-bias and CCP presets use the same direction-editing machinery on other contrasts, but no results are reported for them here.

versions.untested_parts: Direct activation ablation at every layer and position, refusal induction by adding the direction, and retained general abilities are not tested in the reported results.
The README gives refusal counts for selected models and settings only; it does not establish removal across released models generally.
No jailbreak suppression or training-against-ablation robustness results are reported.
The optional multi-direction method is mentioned, but no results compare a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision measures are reported.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer results are reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.
